Base directory for this skill: /Users/merill/.claude/skills/msgraph

# Microsoft Graph Agent Skill

Search, look up, and call any of the 27,700+ Microsoft Graph APIs — all locally, no network calls needed. Use the three search commands to find the right endpoint, check permissions and parameters, then optionally execute calls directly or hand off to a Graph MCP server.

## What's Included

The Microsoft Graph API has **27,700+ endpoints** updated weekly — well past LLM training cutoffs. This skill bundles the complete API surface as local indexes that you search instantly with no network calls.

| Index | Count | What it contains |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAPI endpoints | 27,700+ | Path, method, summary, description, permission scopes |
| Endpoint docs | 6,200+ | Permissions (delegated/app), query parameters, required headers, default vs `$select`-only properties |
| Resource schemas | 4,200+ | All properties with types, supported `$filter` operators, default/select-only flags |
| Community samples | Growing | Hand-verified queries mapping natural-language tasks to exact API calls |

## How to Run

The `msgraph` CLI is bundled with this skill. Run all commands through the launcher script in this skill's directory:

- **macOS / Linux**: `bash <path-to-this-skill>/scripts/run.sh <command> [args...]`
- **Windows**: `powershell <path-to-this-skill>/scripts/run.ps1 <command> [args...]`

For example, to search for mail-related APIs on macOS:

```
bash /home/user/.opencode/skills/msgraph/scripts/run.sh openapi-search --query "send mail"
```

In all examples below, `msgraph` is shorthand for the full launcher invocation.

## Finding the Right API

This is the primary purpose of the skill. Follow this progressive lookup strategy — each level adds detail:

1. **Your own knowledge** — try first for well-known endpoints (`/me`, `/users`, `/groups`).
2. **`sample-search`** — curated, hand-verified samples. Highest quality. Use for common tasks and multi-step workflows.
3. **`api-docs-search`** — per-endpoint permissions, supported query parameters, required headers, default vs `$select`-only properties, and resource property details with filter operators.
4. **`openapi-search`** — full catalog of 27,700 Graph APIs. Use when you cannot find the endpoint any other way.
5. **Reference files** — concept docs on query parameters, advanced queries, paging, batching, throttling, errors, and best practices. Read only when you need specific guidance.

This order is guidance — adapt based on the task. For example, jump straight to `api-docs-search` if you already know the endpoint but need its permissions.

### sample-search

Search curated community samples that map natural-language tasks to exact Microsoft Graph API queries:

```
msgraph sample-search --query "conditional access policies"
msgraph sample-search --product entra
msgraph sample-search --query "managed devices" --product intune
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--query` | Free-text search (searches intent and query fields) |
| `--product` | Filter by product: `entra`, `intune`, `exchange`, `teams`, `sharepoint`, `security`, `general` |
| `--limit` | Max results (default 10) |

At least one of `--query` or `--product` is required. Results include multi-step workflows.

### api-docs-search

Look up detailed documentation for a specific endpoint or resource type:

```
msgraph api-docs-search --endpoint /users --method GET
msgraph api-docs-search --resource user
msgraph api-docs-search --query "ConsistencyLevel"
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint` | Search by endpoint path (e.g. `/users`, `/me/messages`) |
| `--resource` | Search by resource type name (e.g. `user`, `group`, `message`) |
| `--method` | Filter by HTTP method: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` |
| `--query` | Free-text search across all fields |
| `--limit` | Max results (default 10) |

At least one of `--endpoint`, `--resource`, or `--query` is required.

**Endpoint results** include: required permissions (delegated work/school, delegated personal, application), supported OData query parameters, required headers, default properties, and endpoint-specific notes.

**Resource results** include: all properties with types, supported `$filter` operators (eq, ne, startsWith, etc.), and whether each property is returned by default or requires `$select`.

### openapi-search

Search the full OpenAPI catalog of 27,700 Microsoft Graph APIs:

```
msgraph openapi-search --query "send mail"
msgraph openapi-search --resource messages --method GET
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--query` | Free-text search (searches path, summary, description) |
| `--resource` | Filter by resource name (e.g. `users`, `groups`, `messages`) |
| `--method` | Filter by HTTP method |
| `--limit` | Max results (default 20) |

At least one of `--query`, `--resource`, or `--method` is required.

## Using with MCP Servers

If the agent has access to a Microsoft Graph MCP server (such as [lokka.dev](https://lokka.dev) or any other Microsoft Graph MCP server), use the search tools above to find the right endpoint, permissions, and request syntax, then use the information with the MCP server for execution.

In this mode, **no authentication through this skill is needed**. The skill acts purely as a knowledge layer — the MCP server handles authentication and API execution.

## Direct Microsoft Graph API Execution

When no Graph MCP server is available, this skill can authenticate to Microsoft 365 and execute Microsoft Graph API calls directly.

### Authentication

The tool supports **delegated (user)** and **app-only (application)** authentication, auto-detected from environment variables.

**Quick start:**

```
msgraph auth status          # check if signed in
msgraph auth signin          # sign in (opens browser) - recommended
msgraph auth signin --device-code  # sign in via device code (headless)
msgraph auth signout         # clear the session
```

- **Delegated auth** (default): Interactive browser sign-in, with device code fallback for headless environments. Supports incremental consent — on 403, the tool re-authenticates with required scopes and retries automatically.
- **App-only auth**: Auto-detected when `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH`, `MSGRAPH_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`, or `MSGRAPH_AUTH_METHOD=managed-identity` is set. Requires `MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID`.

For detailed authentication configuration including certificates, managed identity, workload identity federation, and all environment variables, see [references/docs/authentication.md](references/docs/authentication.md).

### Making Graph API Calls

**IMPORTANT**: Run `msgraph auth status` before the first `graph-call` in a session to verify authentication.

```
msgraph graph-call <METHOD> <URL> [flags]
```

#### Read Operations

```
msgraph graph-call GET /me
msgraph graph-call GET /users --select "displayName,mail" --top 10
msgraph graph-call GET /me/messages --filter "isRead eq false" --top 5 --select "subject,from,receivedDateTime"
msgraph graph-call GET /users --filter "startsWith(displayName,'John')"
```

#### Write Operations

**IMPORTANT**: YOU MUST ask the user for confirmation before any write operation. Write operations require the `--allow-writes` flag.

```
msgraph graph-call POST /me/sendMail --body '{"message":{"subject":"Hello","body":{"content":"Hi"},"toRecipients":[{"emailAddress":{"address":"user@example.com"}}]}}' --allow-writes
msgraph graph-call PATCH /me --body '{"jobTitle":"Engineer"}' --allow-writes
```

**DELETE is always blocked** regardless of flags.

#### graph-call Flags

| Flag | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `--select` | OData $select | `--select "displayName,mail"` |
| `--filter` | OData $filter | `--filter "isRead eq false"` |
| `--top` | OData $top (limit results) | `--top 10` |
| `--expand` | OData $expand | `--expand "members"` |
| `--orderby` | OData $orderby | `--orderby "displayName desc"` |
| `--api-version` | `v1.0` or `beta` (default: beta) | `--api-version v1.0` |
| `--scopes` | Request additional permission scopes | `--scopes "Mail.Read"` |
| `--headers` | Custom HTTP headers | `--headers "ConsistencyLevel:eventual"` |
| `--body` | Request body (JSON) | `--body '{"key":"value"}'` |
| `--output` | `json` (default) or `raw` | `--output raw` |
| `--allow-writes` | Allow POST/PUT/PATCH (requires user confirmation) | |

## Critical Rules

### Always (search and knowledge)

1. **Never guess or fabricate Microsoft Graph endpoints** — always verify via search before calling. This skill exists because agents hallucinate endpoints; use it.
2. **Use the progressive lookup strategy** — start with what you know, then sample-search, api-docs-search, openapi-search as needed.
3. **Use `--select`** to reduce response size — only request fields you need.
4. **Use `--top`** to limit results — avoid fetching thousands of records.
5. **ConsistencyLevel header** is required for `$count` and `$search` on directory objects (users, groups, etc.). Use `--headers "ConsistencyLevel:eventual"`.
6. **Default API version is beta** — use `--api-version v1.0` for production-stable endpoints.

### When using direct execution (graph-call)

7. **Check auth status** before the first `graph-call` in a session.
8. **GET is the default** — no special flags needed.
9. **Write operations require `--allow-writes`** — YOU MUST confirm with the user first.
10. **DELETE is always blocked** — inform the user this is not supported.
11. **403 triggers automatic re-auth** — the tool requests additional scopes and retries (delegated auth only).
12. **All output is JSON** — parse `statusCode` and `body` fields from the response.

## Error Handling

| Status | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | Token expired | Run `msgraph auth signin` again |
| 403 | Insufficient permissions | Tool auto-retries with incremental consent. If still fails, user needs admin consent. |
| 404 | Resource not found | Verify the endpoint path |
| 429 | Rate limited | Wait for Retry-After duration, then retry |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_ID` | Custom Entra ID app client ID | Microsoft Graph CLI Tools app |
| `MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID` | Target tenant ID (required for app-only) | `common` |
| `MSGRAPH_API_VERSION` | Default API version | `beta` |
| `MSGRAPH_INDEX_DB_PATH` | Path to OpenAPI index database | Auto-detected |

content.content:
### App protection policy evaluation

- **Connect Android devices of version *<supported versions>* to *<MTD partner name>* for app protection policy evaluation**: When you turn on this option, app protection policies that use the "Max allowed threat level" rule evaluate devices by including data from this connector.
- **Connect iOS devices version *<supported versions>* to *<MTD partner name>* for app protection policy evaluation**: When you turn on this option, app protection policies that use the "Max allowed threat level" rule evaluate devices by including data from this connector.

For more information about using Mobile Threat Defense connectors for Intune App Protection Policy evaluation, see [Set up Mobile Threat Defense for unenrolled devices](enable-unenrolled-devices).

### Mobile Threat Defense role

- **Grant MTD role permissions to *<MTD partner name>* on enrolled Android COBO and COPE devices**: When you turn on this option, the selected Mobile Threat Defense partner receives enhanced permissions to help protect enrolled Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed (COBO) and Android Enterprise corporate-owned work profile (COPE) devices from mobile threats.

    On devices where you configure these permissions, the MTD app gets the following exemptions:

    - **Suspension** — The app can't be suspended.
    - **Hibernation** — The app can't enter hibernation.
    - **Power restrictions** — The app is exempt from power-related restrictions such as app standby. The app can start foreground services from the background, and the user can't stop foreground services run by the app.
    - **User controls** — User control over the app is disabled. Users can't clear app data or force-stop the app.

    Important

    Only one MTD partner can hold MTD role permissions per tenant. To use this toggle, first configure the MTD connector for this partner, and target the MTD app to devices through a user or device group.

    Note

    This toggle is available for every [MTD partner](overview#mobile-threat-defense-partners) that supports Android. The same toggle is available on the Defender for Endpoint connector page at **Endpoint security** > **Defender for Endpoint**.

    Applies to:

    - Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed
    - Android Enterprise corporate-owned work profile

    The Mobile Threat Defense role requires devices enrolled through the [Android Management API](https://developers.google.com/android/management). Personally-owned work profiles aren't currently supported.
- **Automatically launch Defender for Endpoint during setup on Android COBO and COPE devices**: This toggle is available only for the Defender for Endpoint connector. When you turn on this option, the Defender for Endpoint app automatically launches during the device setup process on Android Enterprise COBO and COPE devices, allowing Defender for Endpoint to complete its initial configuration without requiring the user to manually open it.

    Note

    This toggle requires that the **Grant MTD role permissions** toggle is also turned on for Defender for Endpoint.

### Shared settings

- **Number of days until partner is unresponsive**: Number of days of inactivity before Intune considers the partner to be unresponsive because the connection is lost. Intune ignores compliance state for unresponsive MTD partners.

Important

When possible, add and assign the MTD apps *before* creating the device compliance and the Conditional Access policy rules. This approach helps ensure that the MTD app is ready and available for end users to install before they can get access to email or other company resources.

Tip

You can see the **Connection status** and the **Last synchronized** time between Intune and the MTD partner from the Mobile Threat Defense pane.

### Integrate compliance with Conditional Access

Conditional Access is a Microsoft Entra capability that works with Intune to help protect devices. For devices that register with Microsoft Entra, Conditional Access policies can use device and compliance details from Intune to enforce access decisions for users and devices.

Combine Conditional Access policy with:

- [Device compliance policies](/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance) can require a device be marked as compliant before that device can be used to access your organization's resources. The Conditional Access policies specify apps services you want to protect, conditions under which the apps or services can be accessed, and the users the policy applies to.
- [App protection policies](../device-security/conditional-access-integration/app-based-policies) can add a security layer that ensures only client apps that support Intune app protection policies can access your online resources, like Exchange or other Microsoft 365 services.

Conditional Access also works with the following to help you keep devices secure:

- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and third-party MTD apps
- Device compliance partner apps
- Microsoft Tunnel

To learn more, see [Learn about Conditional Access and Intune](../device-security/conditional-access-integration/overview).

### Advanced compliance settings

Review the platform specific policies in the Microsoft Intune admin center to identify which compliance settings are available for each platform and more details about their use. To configure policies, see [Create a compliance policy](../device-security/compliance/create-policy).

To configure policies, see [Create a compliance policy](../device-security/compliance/create-policy).

We recommend using the following settings in your enhanced device compliance policies:

When you've integrated Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune, you can use the risk score from Defender as a compliance check. |

content.content:
﻿Ensure at least one **assigned** macOS compliance policy requires a Microsoft Defender machine risk score level.

Microsoft Defender for Endpoint calculates a machine risk score for every onboarded device based on its active alerts and detections. Intune compliance policy can consume that score through **Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score**, so a Mac whose risk rises above an accepted threshold is marked non-compliant and can then be blocked by Conditional Access.

Without this setting the Defender signal never reaches the access decision. A Mac with active high-severity Defender alerts stays compliant and keeps its access to corporate resources, which removes exactly the automatic containment that a Zero Trust architecture assumes is present. Detection without enforcement leaves a compromised endpoint fully trusted.

The threshold accepts **Secured**, **Low**, **Medium** and **High**. The values *unavailable* and *notSet* mean the risk score is not evaluated at all, and neither counts as configured by this test.

Note that a threshold has no effect until the macOS devices are actually onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and the Intune connector is enabled. This test reports whether **Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score** is paired with device threat protection, so a threshold that can never evaluate is visible.

#### Remediation action

1. Navigate to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://intune.microsoft.com).
2. Confirm the Defender for Endpoint connector is enabled under **Endpoint security** > **[Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://intune.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Intune_Workflows/SecurityManagementMenu/~/mdeIntegration)**, and that **Connect macOS devices** is set to **On**.
3. Go to **Devices** > **Manage devices** > **[Compliance](https://intune.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Intune_DeviceSettings/DevicesMenu/~/compliance)**.
4. Select an existing macOS policy, or select **+ Create policy** with **Platform** set to **macOS**.
5. Under **Compliance settings** > **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint**, set **Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score** to **Medium** or stricter.
6. On the **Assignments** tab, assign the policy to your macOS device or user groups.
7. Select **Next** and then **Create** or **Save**.

#### Related links

- [Microsoft Intune admin center - Device compliance](https://intune.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Intune_DeviceSettings/DevicesMenu/~/compliance)
- [Microsoft Learn - Device compliance settings for macOS in Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/compliance/ref-macos-settings)
- [Microsoft Learn - Enforce compliance for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/advanced-threat-protection)
- [Microsoft Learn - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on macOS](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/microsoft-defender-endpoint-mac)

### Defender for Endpoint automatic enrollment is enforced to reduce risk from unmanaged Android threats

If automatic enrollment into Microsoft Defender for Endpoint isn't configured for Android devices in Intune, managed endpoints might remain unprotected against mobile threats. Without Defender onboarding, devices lack advanced threat detection and response capabilities, increasing the risk of malware, phishing, and other mobile-based attacks. Unprotected devices can bypass security policies, access corporate resources, and expose sensitive data to compromise. This gap in mobile threat defense weakens the organization's Zero Trust posture and reduces visibility into endpoint health.

Enabling automatic Defender enrollment ensures Android devices are protected by advanced threat detection and response capabilities. This supports Zero Trust by enforcing mobile threat protection, improving visibility, and reducing exposure to unmanaged or compromised endpoints.

**Remediation action**

Use Intune to configure automatic enrollment into Microsoft Defender for Endpoint for Android devices to enforce mobile threat protection:

- [Integrate Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune and Onboard Devices](/en-us/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration)

### Device cleanup rules maintain tenant hygiene by hiding inactive devices

# Goal `defender-device-risk`: Defender risk in compliance (M2 expert pass)

Mirrors read 2026-11-05. Line numbers are file lines in the mirror. All URLs below were fetched and return 200.

## Summary of changes to the draft

1. **The order is reversed.** Learn connects the services first and onboards devices second. The draft has
   `defender.endpoint-onboarding` → `intune.defender-connector`; it should be connector → onboarding.
2. **Add a missing step**, `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`: the per-platform "Compliance policy
   evaluation" toggles in the connector. Learn treats it as a separate step after the connection, and the risk rule
   doesn't read Defender data on a platform until its toggle is on. ZTA.24871 checks this toggle (Android only),
   not the connection.
3. **MT.1098 does not verify the connector.** It skips when no connectors exist and passes when another vendor's
   connector is healthy and Defender's is missing. It verifies none of this goal's steps.
4. **Of the three draft verifying tests, only MT.1231 fits `intune.compliance-device-risk`.** MT.1235 reads a
   different setting (the third-party MTD "Device Threat Level" on Android device administrator). MT.1216 reads a
   macOS property, but Learn documents no macOS machine-risk compliance setting. Windows is the platform both
   Learn walkthroughs are built around, and no test checks it.
5. `intune.compliance-device-risk` → `intune.compliance-policies` should be **RecommendedFirst**, not Requires.
6. The goal's `Step` is `intune.compliance-device-risk`. The Conditional Access link is made through the goal
   order and the Summary, not through a relationship (see "Goal" below).

Final order: `intune.defender-connector` → `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation` (requires the connector) and
`defender.endpoint-onboarding` (connector recommended first) → `intune.compliance-device-risk` (requires the
evaluation toggles; onboarding and `intune.compliance-policies` recommended first).

## Step 1. `intune.defender-connector` (keep the ID; it moves to first)

- **Title:** Connect Defender for Endpoint to Intune
- **Summary:** Defender for Endpoint and Intune share device data, so Intune can receive the risk level
  Defender gives each device.
- **Relationships:** none. Learn calls it a one-time setup per tenant with no Maester-side prerequisite.
- **Sources**
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration
    (intune-docs-mirror, `intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration.md` L78-111). The
    Intune page shows Connection status Unavailable until the Intune connection toggle is set to On in the Defender
    portal under Advanced features. It then shows Enabled, which can take up to 15 minutes.
    **Note:** "Turn on the Intune connection in the Defender portal's advanced features, then check that Intune
    reports the connection as enabled. The status can lag by about 15 minutes."
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/advanced-features (defender-docs-mirror,
    `defender-endpoint/advanced-features.md` L208-220). The integration has to be enabled in both products, and it
    needs Intune-managed Windows devices that are Entra joined.
    **Note:** "The integration must be switched on in both Defender for Endpoint and Intune before Intune can use
    Defender's device data."
- **Rollout:** none. It is a tenant toggle with no staged option.
- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. MT.1098 reports connector health but skips or passes when the
  Defender connector is missing."
- **New check proposed** (reserve an MT ID on #697): GET `deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors` (beta).
  Pass when the connector `fc780465-2017-40d4-a0c5-307022471b92` (Defender for Endpoint, the ID MT.1098 L55 and
  ZTA.24871 already use) exists with `partnerState = enabled`. It shares the cache with MT.1098.

## Step 2 (new). `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`

- **Title:** Turn on compliance evaluation in the Defender for Endpoint connector
- **Summary:** Compliance policies for Windows, iOS/iPadOS and Android include the risk level that Defender for
  Endpoint reports for those devices.
- **Requires `intune.defender-connector`**
  - configure-integration.md L113-130: after the connection exists, enable "Connect Android / iOS/iPadOS / Windows
    devices to Defender for Endpoint" under Compliance policy evaluation. L130: this connects every applicable
    managed device, and future enrollments, for compliance evaluation.
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/configure-conditional-access (defender-docs-mirror,
    `defender-endpoint/configure-conditional-access.md` L81-94). Step 1 is the connection. Step 2 checks that the
    connection is Enabled and that the Windows compliance-evaluation toggle is On.
  - **Note:** "Once the connection shows Enabled, turn on compliance policy evaluation for each platform in the
    connector settings. Each platform has its own toggle."
- **Rollout:** none. The toggle applies to every managed device on the platform at once (L130).
- **Verifying tests:** ZTA.24871 is narrower (Android only; see the tests section). No Maester test.
- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks Android only (ZTA.24871)."
  A Maester check could read `windowsEnabled`, `iosEnabled` and `androidEnabled` on the same connector record
  (properties confirmed in the Graph `mobileThreatDefenseConnector` schema). It would require each toggle for the
  platforms that have a compliance policy.
- Merging steps 1 and 2 into one step is possible if the owner wants fewer steps. In that case one new check must
  test both conditions, and ZTA.24871 still stays off the step because it covers Android only. I recommend two
  steps: Learn numbers them separately, and they are done in different portals with different roles
  (configure-integration.md L82-85 compared with L117).

## Step 3. `defender.endpoint-onboarding` (keep the ID; it moves after the connector)

- **Title:** Eligible devices are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint. This is a state title, because its only test
  (ZTA.41045) measures coverage.
- **Summary:** Every device that Defender for Endpoint can protect reports to it through a working sensor, so the
  device has a risk level.
- **RecommendedFirst `intune.defender-connector`** (not Requires)
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/onboarding-endpoint-manager (defender-docs-mirror,
    `defender-endpoint/onboarding-endpoint-manager.md` L63-68): the Intune-to-Defender connection is listed as a
    prerequisite for onboarding Windows devices with Intune.
  - configure-integration.md L171-175: the connection gives Intune the onboarding package automatically.
    L229-232 and L246-248: without the connection, the EDR policy accepts only a pasted onboarding blob. So
    onboarding still works without the connection, which is why this is RecommendedFirst. Other onboarding
    methods also exist (`defender-endpoint/configure-endpoints-mdm.md`, "Onboard devices using Microsoft Intune").
  - Intune overview https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/overview
    (`intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/overview.md` L61-62): the connection is step 1 and onboarding
    with Intune policy is step 2.
  - **Note:** "Connect the services first. Intune then receives Defender's onboarding package for its EDR policy,
    and without the connection you must paste an onboarding blob yourself."
- **Rollout**
  - "Assign an Intune EDR onboarding policy to a test device group, and check that the devices appear in the
    Defender portal's device inventory." (onboarding-endpoint-manager.md L75-92; configure-integration.md
    L260-263)
  - "Then assign it to all Windows devices, or deploy the preconfigured policy that targets all devices."
    (configure-integration.md L183-208)
  - "Deploy the Defender app to macOS, Android and iOS/iPadOS devices. Intune has no automatic onboarding package
    for those platforms." (configure-integration.md L164-167, L269-306)
- **Verifying tests:** ZTA.41045 matches (see below). No Maester test.
- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.41045) once its
  results can name steps."
- `OnlyWhen`: the step needs Defender for Endpoint P1, P2 or Business (`MDE_LITE`, `WINDEFATP`, `MDE_SMB`).
  `OnlyWhen` can't express "any one of", so leave it empty and rely on each test's `License` gate. This is worth
  a line in section 4.4 of the design.

## Step 4. `intune.compliance-device-risk` (keep the ID)

- **Title:** Require a Defender for Endpoint machine risk score in compliance policies
- **Summary:** Devices that Defender for Endpoint rates above the allowed risk level are marked noncompliant.
- **Requires `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`**
  - configure-conditional-access.md L89-110: Step 2 (connection Enabled, platform toggle On) comes before Step 3
    (compliance policy with "Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score").

# Goal `defender-device-risk`: Defender risk in compliance (M2 expert pass)

Mirrors read 2026-11-05. Line numbers are file lines in the mirror. All URLs below were fetched and return 200.

## Summary of changes to the draft

1. **The order is reversed.** Learn connects the services first and onboards devices second. The draft has
   `defender.endpoint-onboarding` → `intune.defender-connector`; it should be connector → onboarding.
2. **Add a missing step**, `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`: the per-platform "Compliance policy
   evaluation" toggles in the connector. Learn treats it as a separate step after the connection, and the risk rule
   doesn't read Defender data on a platform until its toggle is on. ZTA.24871 checks this toggle (Android only),
   not the connection.
3. **MT.1098 does not verify the connector.** It skips when no connectors exist and passes when another vendor's
   connector is healthy and Defender's is missing. It verifies none of this goal's steps.
4. **Of the three draft verifying tests, only MT.1231 fits `intune.compliance-device-risk`.** MT.1235 reads a
   different setting (the third-party MTD "Device Threat Level" on Android device administrator). MT.1216 reads a
   macOS property, but Learn documents no macOS machine-risk compliance setting. Windows is the platform both
   Learn walkthroughs are built around, and no test checks it.
5. `intune.compliance-device-risk` → `intune.compliance-policies` should be **RecommendedFirst**, not Requires.
6. The goal's `Step` is `intune.compliance-device-risk`. The Conditional Access link is made through the goal
   order and the Summary, not through a relationship (see "Goal" below).

Final order: `intune.defender-connector` → `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation` (requires the connector) and
`defender.endpoint-onboarding` (connector recommended first) → `intune.compliance-device-risk` (requires the
evaluation toggles; onboarding and `intune.compliance-policies` recommended first).

## Step 1. `intune.defender-connector` (keep the ID; it moves to first)

- **Title:** Connect Defender for Endpoint to Intune
- **Summary:** Defender for Endpoint and Intune share device data, so Intune can receive the risk level
  Defender gives each device.
- **Relationships:** none. Learn calls it a one-time setup per tenant with no Maester-side prerequisite.
- **Sources**
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration
    (intune-docs-mirror, `intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration.md` L78-111). The
    Intune page shows Connection status Unavailable until the Intune connection toggle is set to On in the Defender
    portal under Advanced features. It then shows Enabled, which can take up to 15 minutes.
    **Note:** "Turn on the Intune connection in the Defender portal's advanced features, then check that Intune
    reports the connection as enabled. The status can lag by about 15 minutes."
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/advanced-features (defender-docs-mirror,
    `defender-endpoint/advanced-features.md` L208-220). The integration has to be enabled in both products, and it
    needs Intune-managed Windows devices that are Entra joined.
    **Note:** "The integration must be switched on in both Defender for Endpoint and Intune before Intune can use
    Defender's device data."
- **Rollout:** none. It is a tenant toggle with no staged option.
- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. MT.1098 reports connector health but skips or passes when the
  Defender connector is missing."
- **New check proposed** (reserve an MT ID on #697): GET `deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors` (beta).
  Pass when the connector `fc780465-2017-40d4-a0c5-307022471b92` (Defender for Endpoint, the ID MT.1098 L55 and
  ZTA.24871 already use) exists with `partnerState = enabled`. It shares the cache with MT.1098.

## Step 2 (new). `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`

- **Title:** Turn on compliance evaluation in the Defender for Endpoint connector
- **Summary:** Compliance policies for Windows, iOS/iPadOS and Android include the risk level that Defender for
  Endpoint reports for those devices.
- **Requires `intune.defender-connector`**
  - configure-integration.md L113-130: after the connection exists, enable "Connect Android / iOS/iPadOS / Windows
    devices to Defender for Endpoint" under Compliance policy evaluation. L130: this connects every applicable
    managed device, and future enrollments, for compliance evaluation.
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/configure-conditional-access (defender-docs-mirror,
    `defender-endpoint/configure-conditional-access.md` L81-94). Step 1 is the connection. Step 2 checks that the
    connection is Enabled and that the Windows compliance-evaluation toggle is On.
  - **Note:** "Once the connection shows Enabled, turn on compliance policy evaluation for each platform in the
    connector settings. Each platform has its own toggle."
- **Rollout:** none. The toggle applies to every managed device on the platform at once (L130).
- **Verifying tests:** ZTA.24871 is narrower (Android only; see the tests section). No Maester test.
- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks Android only (ZTA.24871)."
  A Maester check could read `windowsEnabled`, `iosEnabled` and `androidEnabled` on the same connector record
  (properties confirmed in the Graph `mobileThreatDefenseConnector` schema). It would require each toggle for the
  platforms that have a compliance policy.
- Merging steps 1 and 2 into one step is possible if the owner wants fewer steps. In that case one new check must
  test both conditions, and ZTA.24871 still stays off the step because it covers Android only. I recommend two
  steps: Learn numbers them separately, and they are done in different portals with different roles
  (configure-integration.md L82-85 compared with L117).

## Step 3. `defender.endpoint-onboarding` (keep the ID; it moves after the connector)

- **Title:** Eligible devices are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint. This is a state title, because its only test
  (ZTA.41045) measures coverage.
- **Summary:** Every device that Defender for Endpoint can protect reports to it through a working sensor, so the
  device has a risk level.
- **RecommendedFirst `intune.defender-connector`** (not Requires)
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/onboarding-endpoint-manager (defender-docs-mirror,
    `defender-endpoint/onboarding-endpoint-manager.md` L63-68): the Intune-to-Defender connection is listed as a
    prerequisite for onboarding Windows devices with Intune.
  - configure-integration.md L171-175: the connection gives Intune the onboarding package automatically.
    L229-232 and L246-248: without the connection, the EDR policy accepts only a pasted onboarding blob. So
    onboarding still works without the connection, which is why this is RecommendedFirst. Other onboarding
    methods also exist (`defender-endpoint/configure-endpoints-mdm.md`, "Onboard devices using Microsoft Intune").
  - Intune overview https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/overview
    (`intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/overview.md` L61-62): the connection is step 1 and onboarding
    with Intune policy is step 2.
  - **Note:** "Connect the services first. Intune then receives Defender's onboarding package for its EDR policy,
    and without the connection you must paste an onboarding blob yourself."
- **Rollout**
  - "Assign an Intune EDR onboarding policy to a test device group, and check that the devices appear in the
    Defender portal's device inventory." (onboarding-endpoint-manager.md L75-92; configure-integration.md
    L260-263)
  - "Then assign it to all Windows devices, or deploy the preconfigured policy that targets all devices."
    (configure-integration.md L183-208)
  - "Deploy the Defender app to macOS, Android and iOS/iPadOS devices. Intune has no automatic onboarding package
    for those platforms." (configure-integration.md L164-167, L269-306)
- **Verifying tests:** ZTA.41045 matches (see below). No Maester test.
- **Unchecked (proposed):** "No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.41045) once its
  results can name steps."
- `OnlyWhen`: the step needs Defender for Endpoint P1, P2 or Business (`MDE_LITE`, `WINDEFATP`, `MDE_SMB`).
  `OnlyWhen` can't express "any one of", so leave it empty and rely on each test's `License` gate. This is worth
  a line in section 4.4 of the design.

## Step 4. `intune.compliance-device-risk` (keep the ID)

- **Title:** Require a Defender for Endpoint machine risk score in compliance policies
- **Summary:** Devices that Defender for Endpoint rates above the allowed risk level are marked noncompliant.
- **Requires `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`**
  - configure-conditional-access.md L89-110: Step 2 (connection Enabled, platform toggle On) comes before Step 3
    (compliance policy with "Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score").
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/mobile-threat-defense/enable-connector
    (`intune/device-security/mobile-threat-defense/enable-connector.md` L90-91): a platform's compliance policies
    include the connector's data only while that platform's toggle is on.
  - **Note:** "The risk rule reads Defender data for a platform only after that platform's compliance-evaluation
    toggle is turned on in the connector."
- **RecommendedFirst `defender.endpoint-onboarding`**
  - overview.md L61-63: onboarding (step 2) comes before the compliance policy (step 3).
  - configure-conditional-access.md L53 and L65: the setup applies to devices that are onboarded to Defender for
    Endpoint.
  - enable-connector.md L164: where possible, deploy the threat defense app before the compliance and Conditional
    Access rules.
  - Why RecommendedFirst: ZTA.41045 demands 100% coverage, and Requires would block the step until every device is
    onboarded.
  - **Note:** "Onboard devices before adding the risk rule. Only onboarded devices report a risk level, and phones
    need the Defender app installed before the rule applies."
- **RecommendedFirst `intune.compliance-policies`** (the draft had Requires)
  - configure-integration.md L351-353: points people who are new to compliance policies to the general
    create-policy guide first.
  - The risk score is one setting inside a platform policy. Requiring every platform to be covered first (the M1
    step's definition) would block a tenant that has a Windows policy but no Android Enterprise policy. Nothing on
    Learn says the risk rule fails without that coverage.
  - **Note:** "The machine risk score is a setting in each platform's compliance policy. Set up the compliance
    policies themselves before adding it."
- **Source for the Conditional Access link** (this is not a relationship). overview.md L116-118, and
  https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/conditional-access (`defender-endpoint/conditional-access.md`
  L58-62): Intune marks the risky device noncompliant, and Conditional Access does the blocking.
  configure-conditional-access.md L112-127 (Step 4) uses the policy-all-users-device-compliance policy, which is
  `entra.ca-require-compliant-device`.
  **Note:** "A device marked noncompliant for risk loses access only where a Conditional Access policy requires a
  compliant device."
- **Rollout**
  - "Set the threshold to Low, the level Learn suggests for most organizations. High blocks nothing and only
    reports." (configure-integration.md L374-401)
  - "Assign the policy to a test group and confirm its devices report the expected compliance state."
    (configure-conditional-access.md L108-110)
  - "Widen the assignment. If a compliant-device policy is already on, risky devices lose access as soon as they
    are marked noncompliant." (configure-integration.md L343)

### One step or one per platform

Use **one step**, named by one test per platform, for these reasons:

- Learn gives one procedure with a platform choice: configure-integration.md L341-410 with the platform list at
  L358-363, and the "Runtime defenses" row of https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/fundamentals/deploy-compliance-step-3
  (`intune/fundamentals/deploy-compliance-step-3.md` L253).
- A goal has one `Step`, and per-platform steps would split it.
- Under "any failing test means Not done", the failing test already names the platform that is missing.

This holds only under two conditions:

1. **A Windows check must exist before tagging.** Both Learn walkthroughs center on Windows
   (configure-conditional-access.md L53 and L96-101). With MT.1231 alone the step would show Done for a tenant that
   protects only iPhones. Proposed check: an assigned `#microsoft.graph.windows10CompliancePolicy` with
   `deviceThreatProtectionEnabled = true` and `deviceThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` in secured, low or
   medium. On Windows the machine-risk rule is the only threat setting (ref-windows-settings.md L267-281), and the
   Graph type has no `advancedThreatProtection*` property. An Android Enterprise check is also needed
   (`advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` on `androidWorkProfileCompliancePolicy` and
   `androidDeviceOwnerCompliancePolicy`; ref-android-enterprise-settings.md L78-82 and L207-209).
2. **A platform with no compliance policy should make its test Not applicable, not a failure.** Today MT.1231
   (L78-84) and MT.1216 (L63-69) return `$false` when the platform has no compliance policy, so a Windows-only
   tenant could never complete the step. A missing policy belongs to `intune.compliance-policies`. This needs a
   test change (a skip with NotApplicable), and the test's owner should agree to it.

Until both conditions hold, tag MT.1231 only. Leave the step's status partial and say so in the PR.

## Goal

```json
{ "Id": "defender-device-risk", "Title": "Block devices Defender finds at risk",
  "Summary": "Devices that Defender for Endpoint rates as risky become noncompliant, so the compliant-device Conditional Access policy blocks them.",
  "Step": "intune.compliance-device-risk" }
```

Don't add `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` → RecommendedFirst `intune.compliance-device-risk`. It would pull the
whole Defender chain into the `compliant-devices` goal, and Learn's CA page (policy-all-users-device-compliance)
doesn't back it. The reverse relationship would contradict Learn's order: configure-conditional-access.md L110 says
to validate the compliance policy before configuring CA. List this goal after `compliant-devices` in `goals.json`.
If the report should show "leads to: Require compliant devices", that is a new display feature for M3/M4, not a
relationship. The current title, "Defender risk in compliance", is fine too. The suggested title names the outcome.

## Verifying tests (all read)

| Test | Definition of done (from the .ps1) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MT.1098 `tests/maester/intune/Test.MT.1098.ps1` | Every connector returned by `deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors` has `partnerState = enabled` and a heartbeat no older than 1 day (L81-87). | ZTA.24824 | Conditional Access policies block access from noncompliant devices | `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` (compliant-devices goal) |

The catalog has no ZTA test for the Windows, iOS or macOS connector toggles, for EDR policy assignment, or for the
machine risk score in compliance.

1. The Defender connector is enabled (step 1).
2. Compliance evaluation is on for each platform with a compliance policy (step 2). This can share a helper with
   check 1 in `powershell/internal/services/intune/`.
3. A Windows compliance policy requires a machine risk score (step 4).
4. An Android Enterprise compliance policy requires a machine risk score (step 4).

Checks 3 and 4 can extend the existing helpers. `Get-MtMobileCompliancePolicy` leaves the Android Enterprise
fields null today (L127-137).

input.message:
The draft for `defender-device-risk` needs four changes:
- **Order:** it is reversed. Learn connects the services first and onboards second.
- **Missing step:** add `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation`, the per-platform toggles in the connector.
- **MT.1098:** it does not prove the Defender connector exists.
- **Verifying tests:** only one of the three draft tests (MT.1231) actually checks the Defender machine risk score in compliance.

No repository files were edited. The full findings (246 lines, with Learn URLs, mirror line numbers, Notes and Rollout) are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill-github-maester--claude-worktrees-defenders-path-m2-8b8ecc/f8bda74f-6c1f-4f6d-9546-cf4020f4c33b/scratchpad/research/defender-device-risk.md`.

**Proposed steps, in order**
1. `intune.defender-connector`, "Connect Defender for Endpoint to Intune". No relationships.
   - Sources: Intune configure-integration L78-111; Defender advanced-features L208-220 (must be on in both products).
   - Unchecked. A new check is needed: connector `fc780465-2017-40d4-a0c5-307022471b92` exists with `partnerState = enabled`.
2. `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation` (new), "Turn on compliance evaluation in the Defender for Endpoint connector". Requires step 1.
   - Sources: configure-integration L113-130; Defender configure-conditional-access L81-94, where it is a separate Step 2.
   - Unchecked. ZTA.24871 checks it for Android only.
3. `defender.endpoint-onboarding`, a state: "Eligible devices are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint". RecommendedFirst step 1, not Requires.
   - Why not Requires: onboarding-endpoint-manager L63-68 lists the connection as a prerequisite only for onboarding through Intune. Without it, the EDR policy accepts a pasted onboarding blob (configure-integration L229-232, L246-248).
   - Rollout: a test device group first, then all devices, then the Defender app on mobile and macOS.
   - Only ZTA.41045 checks it, and it matches.
4. `intune.compliance-device-risk`, "Require a Defender for Endpoint machine risk score in compliance policies".
   - Requires step 2 (configure-conditional-access L89-110; enable-connector L90-91).
   - RecommendedFirst step 3 (overview L61-63; enable-connector L164).
   - RecommendedFirst `intune.compliance-policies`. The draft had Requires, but nothing on Learn says the change fails without full platform coverage, and Requires would block tenants that lack one platform's policy.
   - Rollout: Low threshold, test group first, then widen (configure-integration L374-401; configure-conditional-access L108-110).

**Goal:** its `Step` should be `intune.compliance-device-risk`.
- Learn says the risk rule only blocks access through the compliant-device CA policy: overview L116-118, Defender conditional-access L58-62, and configure-conditional-access Step 4, which uses policy-all-users-device-compliance.
- I would not add a relationship to `entra.ca-require-compliant-device` in either direction.
  - CA recommending device risk first would pull the whole Defender chain into the `compliant-devices` goal, and Learn's CA page doesn't back it.
  - Device risk pointing at CA would contradict Learn, which validates the compliance policy before CA (L110).
- Instead, list the goal after `compliant-devices` in `goals.json` and say it in the Summary.

**MT.1098 (the design's open question):** it does not fail when the Defender connector is missing.
- With no connectors at all, it skips (L63-65, L88-89).
- If another vendor's connector is healthy and Defender's is absent, it passes.
- It fails only when a connector it finds is not `enabled` or its heartbeat is more than a day old (L81-87).
- So it verifies none of these steps and should name no step. It is a generic health check; enable-connector L160 says Intune ignores compliance data from an unresponsive partner, so a "connectors are responsive" state step could come later.

**Platform tests:**
- **MT.1231 (iOS)** is correct: it reads `advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` and rejects `high`. It fails when there is no iOS policy.
- **MT.1235 (Android)** reads a different setting: `deviceThreatProtectionEnabled`, the third-party threat-defense "Device Threat Level" rule, not Defender's risk score. It reads only Android device administrator, which Learn calls deprecated, so it should name no step here.
- **MT.1216 (macOS)** should not name the step.
  - Learn documents the risk-score compliance setting for Android, iOS/iPadOS and Windows only (overview L98-104, configure-integration L124-126 and L345, deploy-compliance-step-3 L202 and L253). The macOS settings reference has no such setting, on the mirror or the live page.
  - It also counts `high` as configured, which blocks nothing.
  - Its guide links to `learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/advanced-threat-protection`, which returns 404.
  - The test itself needs review.
- **No Windows equivalent exists**, and no test of EDR onboarding policies or the Defender connector exists, in any suite or in ZTA.

**One step or one per platform:** one step, named by one test per platform. That works only if two things change first:
- A Windows check is added: `windows10CompliancePolicy.deviceThreatProtectionEnabled` and `deviceThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel` in secured, low or medium. An Android Enterprise check is also needed.
- MT.1231 and MT.1216 are changed to report Not applicable, not fail, when the platform has no compliance policy. Otherwise a Windows-only tenant can never finish the step.

Until then, tag MT.1231 only.

**ZTA:**
- ZTA.41045 "All eligible endpoints are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint" matches step 3.
- ZTA.24871 "Defender for Endpoint automatic enrollment is enforced to reduce risk from unmanaged Android threats" has a title that suggests onboarding. Its logic checks that the Defender connector is enabled and its Android toggle is on, so it belongs to step 2 (Android only), not to the connector step.
- No other ZTA test covers the connector toggles, EDR policies or the risk score in compliance.

**New checks to reserve on #697:**
1. Defender connector enabled.
2. Per-platform compliance-evaluation toggles.
3. Windows machine risk score in compliance.
4. Android Enterprise machine risk score in compliance.

**One open point:** `OnlyWhen` can't express "any one of `MDE_LITE`, `WINDEFATP` or `MDE_SMB`", so the onboarding step has no licence condition and relies on each test's `License` gate.
